policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv כשאוה and qere כְשׁוֹאָ֨ה are the same lexeme שׁוֹאָה with the consonants transposed, so both yield the ASV's 'as a storm' identically. The only note on PRO.1.27 is 'Or, desolation', classed alternative_rendering: it offers an English synonym for that same word and so cannot distinguish a reading. Nothing in the ASV wording excludes either candidate; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
